{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go",
      "line": 534,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Cleanup logs success paths at Error level and prints full ID lists",
      "body": "CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags call r.log.Error on normal execution, including when no rows are selected, and include the full ids slice. This happens on every batch and will produce error-level log noise and potentially very large log lines even when cleanup is healthy. These logs should be debug or info and should not log full ID lists by default."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go",
      "line": 77,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Cleanup interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute",
      "body": "The cleanup ticker now runs all cleanup jobs every minute instead of every 10 minutes. This affects snapshots, dashboard versions, images, invites, short URLs, query history, and annotations, not just the annotation deadlock fix. This can substantially increase database and filesystem load and may be accidental. If intentional, it should be explained or configurable; otherwise it should be reverted."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go",
      "line": 611,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "SQLite inline ID list is built quadratically",
      "body": "In the SQLite fallback, the IN-list is built by repeatedly assigning values = fmt.Sprintf with the previous full string. This creates and copies a growing string on every iteration, giving O(n^2) allocations and CPU usage for large batches such as 32767 IDs. Use strings.Builder or strings.Join instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go",
      "line": 615,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Non-SQLite bind-parameter limits are not handled",
      "body": "deleteByIDs only special-cases SQLite's parameter limit. PostgreSQL has a 65535 bind-parameter limit, and other databases or drivers may have statement-size limits. If AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize is configured above such a limit, the generated DELETE with one placeholder per ID will fail and cleanup will stop. Chunking deletes by a safe maximum parameter count would make this robust across supported databases."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go",
      "line": 556,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Max-count cleanup can delete rows that are no longer excess",
      "body": "For MaxCount cleanup, IDs are selected with OFFSET MaxCount in one session and deleted in another session without rechecking the current ordering. If newer annotations are deleted between the SELECT and DELETE, the selected older IDs may now be within the newest MaxCount annotations, but they are still deleted. The previous single-statement delete evaluated selection and deletion atomically. If this behavior is acceptable, it should be documented; otherwise the delete should re-validate the condition."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Cleanup logs success paths at Error level and prints full ID lists
findings.body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags call r.log.Error on normal execution, including when no rows are selected, and include the full ids slice. This happens on every batch and will produce error-level log noise and potentially very large log lines even when cleanup is healthy. These logs should be debug or info and should not log full ID lists by default.

findings.title: Cleanup interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The cleanup ticker now runs all cleanup jobs every minute instead of every 10 minutes. This affects snapshots, dashboard versions, images, invites, short URLs, query history, and annotations, not just the annotation deadlock fix. This can substantially increase database and filesystem load and may be accidental. If intentional, it should be explained or configurable; otherwise it should be reverted.

findings.title: SQLite inline ID list is built quadratically
findings.body: In the SQLite fallback, the IN-list is built by repeatedly assigning values = fmt.Sprintf with the previous full string. This creates and copies a growing string on every iteration, giving O(n^2) allocations and CPU usage for large batches such as 32767 IDs. Use strings.Builder or strings.Join instead.

findings.title: Non-SQLite bind-parameter limits are not handled
findings.body: deleteByIDs only special-cases SQLite's parameter limit. PostgreSQL has a 65535 bind-parameter limit, and other databases or drivers may have statement-size limits. If AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize is configured above such a limit, the generated DELETE with one placeholder per ID will fail and cleanup will stop. Chunking deletes by a safe maximum parameter count would make this robust across supported databases.

findings.title: Max-count cleanup can delete rows that are no longer excess
findings.body: For MaxCount cleanup, IDs are selected with OFFSET MaxCount in one session and deleted in another session without rechecking the current ordering. If newer annotations are deleted between the SELECT and DELETE, the selected older IDs may now be within the newest MaxCount annotations, but they are still deleted. The previous single-statement delete evaluated selection and deletion atomically. If this behavior is acceptable, it should be documented; otherwise the delete should re-validate the condition.
